title.narrative: Strengthening Member States’ Capacity for Ocean Research and Sustainable Ocean Governance in the Western Pacific and Adjacent Areas

description.narrative:
The Western Pacific and its adjacent regions are among the most densely populated and economically dynamic areas in the world. The ocean lies at the heart of the region’s social, cultural, and economic development, sustaining the livelihoods, food security, transportation, trade, and well-being of hundreds of millions of people. The region hosts some of the world’s richest marine biodiversity, largest coastal populations, and most productive marine and coastal ecosystems, which are fundamental to regional prosperity and resilience.
At the same time, growing human activities and environmental pressures have placed increasing stress on coastal waters and marine ecosystems, including marine pollution, overfishing, biodiversity and habitat loss, and the impacts of climate change. These challenges underscore the urgent need to strengthen ocean research and enhance research capacity to support evidence-based decision-making and sustainable ocean governance across the region, particularly in advancing the achievement of the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), especially SDG 14 on Life Below Water.
This activity aims to strengthen the research capacity of UN Member States in the Western Pacific and adjacent regions, while contributing to the implementation of the IOC Capacity Development Strategy and supporting regional efforts towards achieving the SDGs and other related international frameworks and agreements.
